column1: # One line per mutant that survives its regression test BECAUSE no input can separate it from the
# original. Columns (tab-separated): key, target, rule, original line (stripped), proof.
# A surviving mutant that is not listed here is a FAILURE of the census; an entry whose key is no
# longer generated is STALE (also a failure). Add an entry only with a proof, never to silence a run.

column5: build_root runs only after the DP2 guard proved ${SUBMODULES_DIR}/${TEST_SUBMODULE} is a directory, so the glob "${SUBMODULES_DIR}"/* always matches at least one entry and never stays the literal pattern; an entry that exists by name but fails -e (a dangling symlink) is linked by the mutant as a dangling link to the same missing target, which the gate sees exactly as it sees the skipped entry (absent). The skip changes no gate input.

the line only floors a value at 1: the original and the mutant differ only when the value is exactly 1, and then both leave it 1 (the mutant assigns 1 to a variable that already holds 1). The line's exit status is never read (host_guard.sh has no set -e, and the next statement runs unconditionally), so no input separates them.

column4: cleanup() { trap '' HUP INT TERM; [ -n "${W:-}" ] && [ -d "${W}" ] && rm -rf -- "${W:?}"; }
column5: the dropped conjunct [ -n "${W:-}" ] is implied by the one kept: [ -d "${W}" ] is false for an empty W, so an empty W skips the rm in both; and W is never unset when cleanup runs, because the EXIT trap is installed (line "trap cleanup EXIT") only after W="$(mktemp -d ...)" succeeded or the script exited (set -u then never fires on ${W}). No input separates them.

column4: cleanup() { trap '' HUP INT TERM; [ -n "${W:-}" ] && [ -d "${W}" ] && rm -rf -- "${W:?}"; }
column5: the dropped conjunct [ -d "${W}" ] only skips the rm when W is not a directory; W is the directory mktemp -d made before the EXIT trap was set (the script exits without the trap when mktemp fails), so it is either still that directory (both run rm) or already gone (the mutant runs `rm -rf` of a missing path, a silent no-op). The exit trap's status is not read: bash keeps the exit status the script was leaving with, and every caller reads only that status and the output, which are the same. Not separable without another process replacing the scratch directory by a non-directory, which is outside the meta-test's inputs.
